title.en: Reference frames and time for orbital scenes

summary: Make the frame an explicit object: the same trajectory drawn in an inertial and a rotating frame looks completely different, and both are correct.
objective: Build a scene where one satellite trajectory can be shown in an inertial frame or in a body-fixed rotating frame, with the frame named in every readout.
intent_signals: Show the same orbit in an inertial frame and in an Earth-fixed frame.
Explain why a ground track drifts westward.
example_prompts: Build an orbit viewer that switches between inertial and body-fixed frames with the frame labelled.
Show a satellite trajectory and its ground track derived from the same states.
negative_signals: Not an ephemeris or mission planning tool: no propagation accuracy, perturbations or manoeuvres are claimed.
Not a source of real satellite positions unless a dataset is supplied and cited.
not_for: Not an ephemeris or mission planning tool: no propagation accuracy, perturbations or manoeuvres are claimed.
Not a source of real satellite positions unless a dataset is supplied and cited.

entities.name: Frame axes
entities.guidance: Draw both frames as visible axis triads anchored at the same origin, since the transformation between them is the subject.

entities.name: Trajectory in two frames
entities.guidance: Draw the same state history in each frame, so the difference is a transformation and not two authored curves.

entities.name: Frame-tagged readouts
entities.guidance: Tag every position, velocity and angle readout with the frame it is expressed in.

state_contract.model: A state history sampled at epochs in one primary frame with a declared common origin, and a time-dependent rotation R(t) to a body-fixed frame. Positions transform as r_body = R r_primary, while velocities require the derivative term, v_body = R v_primary plus the derivative of R applied to r_primary. Each historical sample is transformed with the rotation at its own epoch, never with the current orientation. The epoch and time system are stated, and no propagation accuracy is claimed.
state_contract.authority: The primary-frame states are authoritative; the alternative view is a transformation of the same data, never a separately authored path.
actions: Scrub time and watch the body-fixed view rotate.
Toggle the ground track derived from the same states.

invariants: Switching frames never changes the stored state history. Positions rotate with R at each sample epoch, and any velocity shown in the rotating frame includes the frame-rate term; a velocity rotated by R alone is a defect.
Every numeric readout names its frame; an unlabelled coordinate is treated as an error.
The ground track is derived from the same states, using a declared sphere or ellipsoid, a stated longitude convention and explicit seam handling at the antimeridian.
motion_guidance: Animate the frame change as a rotation over a short interval so the viewer sees the transformation rather than a cut.
Advance time at a stated ratio with the epoch and elapsed time visible.
known_limits: Frame conventions and time systems are numerous; a scene must state exactly which ones it implements.
This recipe covers presentation and transformation, not orbit determination or propagation accuracy.
Frame and time-system labels do not by themselves implement a precise rotation model; the scene names the rotation model it uses and keeps the no-propagation-accuracy limit.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Space geometry software distinguishes inertial frames such as an Earth mean equator and equinox frame, which do not rotate with respect to the star background, from body-fixed frames such as an Earth rotating frame, and requires the frame to be named when a state is requested.
claims.scope: Frame vocabulary and the requirement to specify a frame as documented; the scene must state the specific frames it implements.

source_refs.locator: Frames Required Reading, inertial and body-fixed frames and frame specification

object_craft.structure: Two labelled axis triads with distinct shaft profiles so they remain distinguishable when nearly aligned.
object_craft.material: One reserved accent per frame with strong value separation; labels are opaque plates.
object_craft.articulation: The body-fixed triad rotates with the modelled body rotation rate.

object_craft.structure: A tube along the state history with time ticks, drawn from the same samples in either frame.
object_craft.material: Identical trajectory material in both frames so the viewer attributes differences to the frame, not to styling.
object_craft.articulation: Rebuilt on frame switch from the same underlying samples.

physical_contract.scope: Frame transformation and presentation of supplied or authored states; no force model or propagation.
checks: Frame switching preserves the state history exactly.
Every readout displays its frame label.
